references.text: The parallel text in Matthew where Jesus uses the same image of the homeowner and the thief: "But know this, that if the master of the house had known at what watch the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake" ([ref:Matt 24:43-44|Matthew 24:43-44]). This is the closest parallel to Luke 12:39.

Paul uses the same image of a thief coming at night to describe the day of the Lord: "The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night" ([ref:1 Tess 5:2-4|1 Thessalonians 5:2-4]). This connects Jesus' parable to the eschatological expectation of his return.

Peter repeats the image of the thief: "The day of the Lord will come like a thief" ([ref:2 Pet 3:10|2 Peter 3:10]). The motif of the Lord's unexpected coming as a thief originates from Jesus' teaching in Luke 12:39.

In the letter to the church in Sardis, Jesus says: "If you do not stay awake, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come upon you" ([ref:Åp 3:3|Revelation 3:3]). The thief metaphor is used here as a direct warning to be vigilant.

In the midst of describing the final plagues, Jesus says: "Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who stays awake" ([ref:Åp 16:15|Revelation 16:15]). The same image of the thief coming unexpectedly, with a blessing attached to vigilance.

The immediate context before verse 39, where Jesus urges the disciples to be ready with girded loins and burning lamps, waiting for their master ([ref:Luk 12:35-38|Luke 12:35-38]). The parable of the thief in verse 39 reinforces this message of readiness.

The verse immediately following, which gives the direct application of the parable: "Be ready also! For the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect" ([ref:Luk 12:40|Luke 12:40]). The point of the thief parable is explained explicitly here.

In Mark's eschatological discourse, Jesus exhorts: "Be on guard, stay awake! For you do not know when the time will be" ([ref:Mark 13:33-35|Mark 13:33-35]). The same fundamental theme of not knowing the timing and the necessity of vigilance.

Old Testament legislation concerning burglary (breaking through a wall): "If the thief is caught while breaking in (חתרת)..." ([ref:2 Mos 22:1-2|Exodus 22:1-2]). The word διορυχθῆναι (to dig/break through) in Luke 12:39 reflects the ancient practice of breaking through mud walls, which is also the background for this Old Testament text.
